metadata.goal: Analyze how the courier organizes delivery tasks across space and time, and identify the main operational patterns or trade-offs that shape the route.
metadata.dataset_description: Twenty delivery tasks and a timestamped courier trajectory expose cluster transitions, deadlines, completion order, remaining workload, and delivery pace.

insight_list.insight: The courier follows a strongly area-oriented strategy, completing most nearby tasks consecutively before moving to another service cluster, with very few returns to previously visited areas.

plot.title: Area-Oriented Completion Sequence
plot.description: Tasks are labeled by completion order and colored by service cluster.

insight_list.question: How does the courier sequence nearby tasks across service clusters, and how often does the route return to a previously served area?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Compare consecutive completion labels and cluster transitions.
insight_list.code:
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
d=df.sort_values('completion_sequence'); print(d[['completion_sequence','service_cluster']]); plt.scatter(d.task_x_km,d.task_y_km,c=pd.Categorical(d.service_cluster).codes); plt.show()

insight_list.insight: An otherwise compact task sequence is interrupted by a geographically isolated task with a much earlier deadline; after completing it, the courier returns to the original service area.

plot.title: Early-Deadline Spatial Interruption
plot.description: The map and deadline-slack panel isolate the urgent detour and return to area A.

insight_list.question: Which task interrupts the compact area sequence, and what deadline and spatial evidence explains the detour and return?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Relate completion order to task location and deadline slack.
insight_list.code:
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
d=df.copy(); d['deadline']=pd.to_datetime(d.deadline); d['completion_time']=pd.to_datetime(d.completion_time); d['slack_min']=(d.deadline-d.completion_time).dt.total_seconds()/60; print(d.nsmallest(3,'slack_min')[['task_id','service_cluster','completion_sequence','slack_min']]); plt.scatter(d.completion_sequence,d.slack_min); plt.show()

insight_list.insight: Task completion is rapid while orders remain densely clustered, but the delivery pace slows markedly near the end of the route as the remaining tasks become fewer and more spatially dispersed.

plot.title: Pace versus Remaining Tasks
plot.description: Time between consecutive task completions is shown against the declining number of pending tasks.

insight_list.question: How does delivery pace change as the route approaches its final, spatially dispersed tasks?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Compare inter-completion intervals with pending-task count and completion phase.
insight_list.code:
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
d=df[df.completion_sequence>1]; plt.scatter(d.pending_tasks_before_completion,d.inter_completion_minutes,c=d.completion_sequence); plt.gca().invert_xaxis(); plt.show(); print(d.groupby(d.completion_sequence>14).inter_completion_minutes.median())

insights: The courier follows a strongly area-oriented strategy, completing most nearby tasks consecutively before moving to another service cluster, with very few returns to previously visited areas.
An otherwise compact task sequence is interrupted by a geographically isolated task with a much earlier deadline; after completing it, the courier returns to the original service area.
Task completion is rapid while orders remain densely clustered, but the delivery pace slows markedly near the end of the route as the remaining tasks become fewer and more spatially dispersed.
summary: The route is mostly organized cluster by cluster, with one early-deadline task causing the only clear return to a previous area. Completion remains fast through dense clusters and slows as the final tasks become sparse and geographically dispersed.
